chunks: Al-Husayn narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the place of the forehead of the one prostrating: should it be higher than his seat? He said, 'No, but it should be level.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct position of the forehead during prostration in Shia Islamic prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the physical mechanics of sujood, emphasizing that the forehead must rest evenly on the prostration surface rather than being elevated, which ensures the humility and completeness of the bowing posture. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential focus on the precise physical manifestation of reverence (khushu) during prayer, distinguishing valid prostration from mere bending. It reflects the broader principle that the external form of worship must align with the internal state of submission.
